candidates.name: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
support_spans: Biliary stricture biopsy: Consistent with adenocarcinoma
CT abdomen/pelvis: 2.6 × 3.1 cm pancreatic head mass with associated pancreatic ductal dilatation
candidates.why: The patient has a pancreatic head mass and a biliary stricture biopsy consistent with adenocarcinoma.

candidates.name: Rhabdomyolysis
support_spans: Initial creatinine kinase (CK) level: 22,000 IU/L, later peaked at >40,000 IU/L
Right biceps femoris biopsy: Nonspecific myopathic changes consistent with rhabdomyolysis
candidates.why: The patient has significantly elevated CK levels and a muscle biopsy consistent with rhabdomyolysis.

candidates.name: Statins-induced rhabdomyolysis
support_spans: He had been taking atorvastatin as a home medication.

candidates.why: The patient was taking atorvastatin, a statin known to cause rhabdomyolysis in rare cases.

candidates.name: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma with paraneoplastic necrotizing myopathy
support_spans: Cancer antigen 19-9 level: 2930 kU/L
CT abdomen/pelvis: 2.6 × 3.1 cm pancreatic head mass with associated pancreatic ductal dilatation
contradict_spans: Pancreatic head biopsy: Hypocellular with scant atypical cells
candidates.why: The patient's presentation with jaundice, weight loss, and abdominal pain, along with the elevated cancer antigen 19-9 level and pancreatic head mass, suggests pancreatic adenocarcinoma, which can be associated with paraneoplastic necrotizing myopathy, explaining the muscle weakness and elevated creatinine kinase level.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may deserve minority protection because paraneoplastic syndromes are rare and easily missed, and the pancreatic head biopsy results may not have captured the full extent of the tumor.

candidates.name: Rhabdomyolysis due to statin-induced myopathy
support_spans: He had been taking atorvastatin as a home medication.
Initial creatinine kinase (CK) level: 22,000 IU/L, later peaked at >40,000 IU/L
contradict_spans: Right biceps femoris biopsy: Nonspecific myopathic changes consistent with rhabdomyolysis, but not specifically indicating statin-induced myopathy
candidates.why: The patient's long-term use of atorvastatin, a statin known to cause myopathy, along with the elevated creatinine kinase level and muscle weakness, suggests statin-induced myopathy as a possible cause of rhabdomyolysis.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may deserve minority protection because statin-induced myopathy is a rare but potentially serious side effect that may be overlooked in patients with multiple comorbidities.
